title: Trump mega-donors holding stakes in companies that received federal backing
summary: Paulson is the clearest case. He is a documented Trump fundraiser and the largest holder of Perpetua, which won a $2.9B EXIM loan approval (not yet closed). He also gained an estimated $60-70M on paper from the Trilogy stake before selling out in Q4 2025. Context: much of Perpetua's federal support began under Biden. Yass ($16M to MAGA Inc.) and Boehly ($1M+) are documented donors whose holdings sit in a federally approved TikTok venture and a DFC-backed Lukoil bid. That bid is pending and unsigned. The rest is weaker. The Schwarzman/Griffin/Cohen PIPE purchase rests on one Senate letter, Griffin is a public critic, and no Cohen donation to Trump was found. Warren and Hamm got regulatory help, not stakes, loans or price floors. No realised donor windfall is documented apart from Paulson's undisclosed Trilogy sale.

sub_claims.statement: John Paulson (Trump fundraiser) is Perpetua Resources' largest shareholder, and Perpetua won a $2.9B EXIM loan approval in 2026.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented. This extends C77. Paulson hosted Trump's April 2024 Palm Beach fundraiser ($50.5M raised) and was considered for Treasury Secretary. Paulson & Co. bought $100M of Perpetua's ~$425M June 2025 raise at $13.20 a share. Bloomberg Government says he has put about $185M into the company in total. 13F trackers put Paulson & Co. at 32.3M shares, about 25-26% of Perpetua, in Q1 2026, the largest holder by a wide margin (audit re-check; aggregator figures). Under Trump: Stibnite became a FAST-41 priority project in April 2025, received its final Army Corps permit in May 2025, and won EXIM board approval for $2.9B in May 2026 (EXIM had notified Congress of $2.7B in March 2026). The loan is still subject to definitive documents and conditions precedent (expected in H2 2026 per the May 2026 announcement), and no final close was found through Nov 2026. Context that cuts the other way: the Forest Service record of decision (2025-01-03), the first ~$1.8B EXIM letter of interest (April 2024) and most of the ~$80M in DoD awards all came under Biden. Paper gain: our own arithmetic, not a sourced figure. The roughly 7.58M June 2025 placement shares were worth about $203M at the 2026-05-21 close of US$26.72, a paper gain of about $100M on that tranche alone. No Paulson statement on a conflict was found.

sub_claims.statement: Paulson profited from the October 2025 U.S. stake in Trilogy Metals and later sold out.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented. Paulson & Co. held about 8.7% of Trilogy (fourth-largest holder). On 2025-10-06 the Department of War signed a binding letter of intent to pay $35.6M in total for about 10% of Trilogy, in two parallel halves: $17.8M directly to Trilogy for 8,215,570 units at $2.17 (each with three-quarters of a warrant), and $17.8M to South32 for 8,215,570 existing Trilogy shares plus a call option on 6,161,678 more; all $35.6M is to be reinvested in Ambler Metals. The warrants and option could take the stake toward 17.5%. The administration also approved the Ambler Road. The stock rose more than 200%. Popular Information and Dermot Cole estimated Paulson's paper gain at $60-70M. His 13F shows he sold all 14.3M shares between 2025-10-01 and 2025-12-31. The exact dates and prices are not disclosed, so the realised gain is unknown. Paulson has not explained the sale. Context: the largest holder, Thomas Kaplan's Electrum (~18.5%, worth >$136M in March 2026), gained more on paper. We found no reporting that describes Kaplan as a Trump donor, and his giving was not checked.

sub_claims.statement: Paulson's other big 2025 bet, Donlin Gold (Alaska), received federal backing.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented holding, but no federal backing found. Paulson paid Barrick $800M for 40% of Donlin (closed 2025-06-03). On 2026-07-21 NovaGold agreed to buy that 40% in an all-stock deal valued at about $4.2B, leaving Paulson with about 40% of the economic interest in the combined NovaGold Corp. The deal is expected to close in Q4 2026. The only federal action we found is a court-ordered Army Corps supplemental environmental review. We found no federal equity stake, loan or price floor. Separately, Paulson gave $250,000 to MAGA KY, a Trump-allied super PAC (2025). We did not find a Paulson MAGA Inc. contribution.

sub_claims.statement: Schwarzman, Griffin and Steven A. Cohen, as Trump allies, bought discounted shares in the Cantor-placed USA Rare Earth PIPE that sat alongside the Commerce stake.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source allegation for the share purchases. The senators' 2026-02-26 letter is the only source, and the company's PIPE release names only Inflection Point. The donor links vary. Schwarzman: documented. He gave $5M to MAGA Inc. in H2 2025 (FEC, via Bloomberg on 2026-01-02) and also donated to the White House ballroom. Griffin: he gave $1M to the inauguration and met Trump in 2024, but did not endorse him. In January 2026 he publicly accused the administration of being 'very enriching to the families' of officials, so calling him a 'Trump ally' is contestable. Citadel did hold about 5.6M USAR shares in Q3 2026 (C77), but a 13F does not show PIPE participation. Cohen: we found no Trump or MAGA Inc. donation. His documented Trump-family link runs instead through Point72's 4% stake in Alt5 Sigma, the WLF treasury vehicle (Bloomberg, 2025-08-19; see C13). Gains: the PIPE price was $21.50 and the stock was about $9.30 in late October 2026, so any PIPE buyer had a paper loss. Cantor says it had no role in USAR's government deal.

sub_claims.statement: Todd Boehly, a Trump donor, leads a bid for Lukoil's foreign assets in which a federal agency (DFC) would take equity.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented donations; consortium single-source (FT, relayed by several outlets). Eldridge Industries (Boehly) gave $1M to Trump's inaugural. NBC's FEC analysis lists Boehly among new $1M+ MAGA Inc. donors after the 2024 election, but the exact amount and date could not be confirmed because the article was not read directly. The FT reported in September 2026 that Boehly's consortium for Lukoil International includes Tahnoon-chaired IHC, the Qatari Al-Khayyat family and the U.S. DFC, which would take a reported mid-teens equity stake. As of the latest OFAC extension (2026-10-21), the license runs to 2026-11-21 and covers negotiations only. No deal was signed and no DFC commitment was announced. Nothing has been realised. C76 covers the Witkoff/Kushner side and their denials.

sub_claims.statement: Kelcy Warren (Energy Transfer) got federal backing after giving to Trump.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented donations and regulatory actions; the benefit is regulatory, not an equity stake, loan or price floor. Warren gave at least $5M toward Trump's 2024 bid. Warren and Energy Transfer together gave MAGA Inc. $25M in February 2025 (Forbes reports $12.5M each). Under Biden, DOE refused to extend Lake Charles LNG's export deadline and denied rehearing. On day one, Trump lifted the Biden LNG-export pause, and in August 2025 Energy Secretary Wright granted Lake Charles more time to start non-FTA exports. Energy Transfer then suspended the project on 2025-12-18, so no gain flowed from it. Energy Transfer had called the earlier DOE denial 'political'.

sub_claims.statement: Harold Hamm (Continental Resources) got federal stakes, loans or price floors.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented donations and role; financial backing not found. Hamm gave $3,300 to Trump's campaign in 2023, plus $1.6M-$4.3M to pro-Trump committees (figures from advocacy sources, which disagree). He chaired energy policy on the 2024 transition and was named a White House ballroom donor in October 2025. High Country News and the Revolving Door Project describe BLM approving Continental permits, including 71 new wells in one county. We found no federal equity stake, loan or price floor for Continental. Continental did not comment.

sub_claims.statement: Jeff Yass, a top MAGA Inc. donor, holds ByteDance and is in the federally approved TikTok USDS joint venture.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented. Yass gave MAGA Inc. $16M: $1M days before the inauguration and $15M in March 2025. In 2024 his spokesperson had said he had never given to Trump. Susquehanna is reported to own about 15% of ByteDance and Yass about 7% personally; outlet valuations vary widely. Trump reversed his position to oppose a TikTok ban after meeting Yass in March 2024, but no source shows the meeting caused the change. Trump repeatedly delayed enforcing the ban, approved the framework by executive order on 2025-09-25, and the joint venture closed on 2026-01-22. Susquehanna affiliate Vastmere Strategic Investments is an investor (one outlet attributes Vastmere to Dell instead), and SIG's Mark Dooley holds a board seat. ByteDance retains 19.9%. Gains are undisclosed. Earlier layers: Susquehanna held about 2% of DWAC before the TMTG merger and says it had no economic interest as a market maker. Reuters (2026-10) also named it as a Truth Social API subscriber (C41).

sub_claims.statement: Congress has asked whether Trump donors hold equity in companies receiving federal equity stakes.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (a question, not a finding). On 2026-02-02, House Natural Resources Democrats asked DoD, Commerce, Energy and Interior whether major Trump campaign donors or Trump Organization affiliates hold equity in companies the government has invested in. Fortune (2026-07-26) found no single public ledger of the roughly $27B in federal stakes, and several of them, such as Vulcan Elements and xLight, have no SEC filings. No agency answer was found.

corrections: The claim calls Griffin a Trump ally. He gave $1M to the inauguration but did not endorse Trump in 2024, and in 2026 he publicly accused the administration of enriching officials' families.
We found no Trump or MAGA Inc. donation from Steven A. Cohen. His documented Trump-family link is Point72's 4% Alt5 Sigma stake.
Perpetua's federal backing did not begin under Trump. The record of decision, the first EXIM letter of interest ($1.8B, April 2024) and most of the DoD awards came under Biden.
Kelcy Warren and Harold Hamm received regulatory decisions (an LNG deadline extension, BLM permits), not federal equity stakes, loans or price floors. Lake Charles LNG was suspended in December 2025.
Trilogy's biggest paper winner was Electrum (~18.5%), not Paulson (~8.7%).

2026-11-17: ballroom donor list. The Adelson Family Foundation (a US family foundation; not Israeli government or company money) is reported to have committed $25M to the White House ballroom, the top tier alongside Nvidia, Apple and Charles Ergen, per a Washington Post list of donor records relayed by the Boston Globe (16 Oct 2026). Single-source: one outlet's records, and the foundation did not comment. Neither this check nor the donor list it relied on carried an amount for the foundation, and no sentence here ties a donation to any decision. Details are in C110.
denials_and_context: Cantor says it had no role in USA Rare Earth's government negotiations or financing.
Paulson has not explained his Trilogy sale. An economist quoted by the Alaska Beacon said the sale does not necessarily signal anything.
In 2024 Yass's spokesperson said he had never donated to Trump. In 2025 he gave $16M to MAGA Inc. Susquehanna says it had no economic interest in Trump Media and held DWAC only as a market maker.
Witkoff's spokesperson denies any conflict in the Lukoil talks (C76). No Boehly or DFC statement was found.
Energy Transfer called the Biden-era DOE denial 'political'. Continental did not respond to requests for comment.
A documented donation plus a federal action is not evidence of a quid pro quo. No source shows that any donation caused any federal decision.

Trilogy: upheld (8.7%, 14.3M shares sold in Q4 2025 per Bloomberg/13F; dates and prices undisclosed). Clarified that the $35.6M was split: only $17.8M went to Trilogy; the other $17.8M bought existing shares from South32. Relationship label updated.

TikTok/Yass: upheld. Vastmere Strategic Investments is named as a Susquehanna affiliate and SIG's Mark Dooley holds one of seven board seats; Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX hold 15% each and ByteDance 19.9%. Sources still disagree on the residual 'other investors' share; no change needed.
Label check: Paulson's ~$100M Perpetua paper gain is marked as our arithmetic; the USAR PIPE purchases are marked single-source; the Boehly consortium is marked single-source (FT).
